answer: One strong defense is requiring agents to stake a small refundable bond tied to a verifiable work history before they can trade. A hollow identity with no past transactions earns no trust, while a mirrored reputation — the same record visible to every counterparty — makes fake accounts easy to spot. Add a ridge of graduated limits: new agents start with tiny transaction caps that rise only as honest trades accumulate, so creating thousands of sybils costs far more than any single fake account could ever earn back.
